mistakes.forge_default: MAIN2 (escalated): cast Walking Ballista from graveyard via Creature lane

Then with 3 mana, Forge passed and Jev agreed (p=0.36, not gated) while Spore Frog was offered but tagged CantPlayAi; the start-of-turn memo said to cast Frog. After the escalation memo said 'Cast Spore Frog from the graveyard (creature lane)', Jev still lacked the 0.15 margin over Forge's Ballista.

mistakes.evidence: [t30 block] b1 Sauron 7/6: OVERRULE p=0.49 pF=0.3 F no block -> block with Muldrotha 6/6; b0 Army: default 'k-1' (not an option) -> block with Spore Frog

mistakes.forge_default: Bloodstained Mire fetch: Zagoth Triome (enters tapped)

The agreed Triome fetch made Muldrotha unaffordable, so it was never offered (the downstream not_offered is a consequence). Jev then overruled Forge's Ballista to cast Doc, overruled again for Eternal Witness, and overruled Witness's target from Grist (F) to Verdant Catacombs.

systematic.pattern: Unhooked sacrifice costs: the pilot picks 'activate X: Sacrifice a permanent' but Forge silently picks what to sacrifice, and it picks lands
systematic.count_or_examples: Forge logs, pods 01-03, our seat: Claws of Gix 11 of 13 sacrifices were lands (the other 2 were Claws itself); Barrin 8 of 11 were lands (the rest: Kaya's Ghostform, Dalek Drone, Barrin itself); Braids's end-step trigger (asked only yes/no) 6 of 12 were lands, 2 were Sol Ring, 1 was Braids herself. That's 25 lands lost to cost payments in 12 games. A factor in 7 reviewed mistakes, including 3 game-losing ones (the primary mechanism in 2 of those): pod01-g2 t42 (six lands in one turn; Jev re-activated Claws 6 times), pod03-g3 t44, pod03-g3 t36 (Ghostform sacrificed instead of the Ghostformed Drone), pod03-g1 t35, pod03-g1 t31, pod01-g4 t38, pod02-g1 t22.
systematic.why_it_matters: The memo's plans hinge on 'sacrifice the spent X'. Jev can't express that and can't see the result, so it keeps activating (6x on pod01-g2 t42). Either hook the cost choice as a question or name Forge's intended sacrifice in the option text.

systematic.pattern: Unhooked X: Forge picks X for spells Jev forced through a CantPlayAi tag
systematic.count_or_examples: Toxic Deluge: 3 of 3 casts in pods 01-03 resolved at X≈0 (pod01-g4 t35, pod02-g3 t28, pod03-g4 t16; memos said X=5, 10, 4), all after Jev overruled Forge's pass. Pernicious Deed: 3 of 3 activations used X = all available mana (pod01-g2 t40 X=7, which killed our Muldrotha when the memo said X=4; pod03-g2 t16 X=1; pod03-g4 t24 X=2). The Deed and Deluge option text never shows X.
systematic.why_it_matters: It is the primary mechanism of 4 reviewed mistakes (1 game-losing, pod02-g3 t28) and a factor in 3 more (pod01-g3 t36, pod03-g2 t16, pod03-g4 t24), where Deed X would have been Forge's anyway. Forge's own X logic rejected the spell in the first place, so letting it choose X after an overrule is close to a guaranteed misplay. X (and Ballista's counter count) needs to be part of the option or a follow-up question.

systematic.pattern: Main-phase-1 'hold' default with every play tagged CantPlayAi; Forge then plays in main 2
systematic.count_or_examples: 228 MAIN1 action questions where Forge's default was pass and every non-land option carried a "Forge's heuristic AI would not do this" tag (99 agreed, 39 gated, 90 overruled). In 61 turns main 1 ended in a pass with 2+ mana; in 55 of those, Forge's first main-2 default was a play. Reviewed cases: pod03-g2 t49 (game-losing: three graveyard removal spells skipped, GATED p=0.14, then attack), pod02-g2 t39 (GATED p=0.09, then Forge's Vrock ate the creature lane in main 2), pod01-g2 t12, pod02-g1 t26, pod02-g4 t24, pod01-g1 t42.
systematic.why_it_matters: Removal-before-combat lines are decided against a 'pass' default carrying tags that discourage every play. When Jev doesn't clear 0.15, the turn's plan moves to main 2, where Forge's own play becomes the default and uses up the lane or mana the memo needed.

systematic.pattern: Duplicated Muldrotha lane options (identical text, or '(Creature)' vs '(Artifact)' suffixes) blur overrule and gate records and probably dilute Jev's probability
systematic.count_or_examples: 135 of 887 action questions contain identical-text duplicates; 159 list the same graveyard card 2+ times. 12 logged 'overrules' were Jev choosing an identical-text twin of Forge's option (e.g. pod01-g1 t42 Capsule; pod03-g1 t23 Sol Ring). 13 of 91 gated records had a same-play twin of Forge's default, so 'gated' may mean Jev wanted the same play (pod01-g1 t42 Ballista, pod02-g2 t39 Vrock, pod03-g2 t47 Ghostform at p=0.06, pod01-g3 t36 Hostage Taker, and Muldrotha casts from the command zone listed 3x). Lane conflicts are never surfaced: Capsule took the artifact lane Ballista needed (pod01-g1 t42), and Ghostform took the enchantment lane Galactus needed (pod03-g2 t47).
systematic.why_it_matters: It inflates overrule counts, makes gated records uninterpretable (Jev's pick isn't logged), and probably splits Jev's mass across twins, so its top option clears the margin less often. Dedupe identical options, name the lane explicitly, and log Jev's raw pick on gated records.

systematic.pattern: Mulligan preferences are inverted relative to land count, and there's no memo at mulligan time
systematic.count_or_examples: Pods 01-03: all 4 Jev mulligan overrules went the wrong way. pod02-g4 shipped a 4-land 7 and kept a 1-land 7; pod03-g4 shipped a 5-land 7 and kept a 1-land 6. Among the gated mulligans, Jev wanted to ship three 3-4-land hands (pod02-g3, pod03-g2, pod03-g3) and to keep a 0-land hand (pod03-g4). Across all 6 pods, 10 of 10 mulligan overrules are inverted (e.g. pod05-g4 and pod06-g2 kept 0-landers).
systematic.why_it_matters: 2 reviewed mistakes (pod02-g4, pod03-g4) and several slow starts. Jev appears unable to count lands from a bare card list. Give the prompt an explicit land/ramp count, or don't let Jev overrule mulligans.

systematic.pattern: Attack and block prompts carry no board context; Jev's attack overrules lean toward the low-life defender
systematic.count_or_examples: 15 attack overrules (Forge 'don't attack' -> Jev attack) in pods 01-03; reviewers flagged 8 of them (pod01-g4 t35, pod02-g2 t45 x2, pod02-g3 t24 and t32, pod03-g2 t30 and t49 x2), 2 game-losing. Most were aimed at the lowest-life player (P1 at 2, 3, 6 life) into untapped blockers the option text doesn't mention. In 2 block questions Forge's default blocker id 'k-1' (e.g. Baleful Strix) wasn't among the options (pod01-g1 t30, pod03-g1 t36).
systematic.why_it_matters: The only information in 'attack P1 (2 life)' is the life total, which makes attacking look free. Adding untapped potential blockers and crack-back power per defender would give Jev the context the memos assume.

systematic.pattern: Fetch and shock lands enter tapped because the shock payment is silent and the fetch pick ignores the plan's mana need
systematic.count_or_examples: 10 of 27 fetch activations in pods 01-03 produced no mana this turn (a Triome, or a shockland with Forge declining the 2 life), though an untapped basic or dual was offered every time (6 agreed with Forge, 2 gated, 2 Jev overrules). This made the memo's key spell unaffordable, so it never appeared in the options, at pod01-g1 t33 (Muldrotha), pod03-g1 t35 (Massacre Wurm, game-losing) and pod03-g2 t47; a hand-played Watery Grave did the same at pod03-g3 t57 (Dellian).
systematic.why_it_matters: It turns into a silent 'not_offered' downstream, and the memo's mana counts ('crack for a basic Swamp, untapped: 8 mana') are never checked. Hooking the shock payment and adding 'enters tapped / untapped this turn' to fetch options would fix most cases.

systematic.pattern: Some triggers and abilities are never offered
systematic.count_or_examples: The Coming of Galactus chapter I ('destroy up to one target') was asked 0 of 4 times in pods 01-03 (Binding the Old Gods chapter I was asked 2 of 2); pod02-g2 t45 hit Wight instead of the memo's Lyra, and pod01-g1 t42 hit Sephiroth instead of Bitterblossom. Otawara's Channel was missing from every action list on pod01-g4 t28, t32 and t35 while in hand. At pod01-g4 t38, Barrin's second activation and the Otawara channel vanished after the first bounce with 7 mana up. Shriekmaw was absent at pod03-g3 t60.
systematic.why_it_matters: Memos build lines on actions the pilot can't take. The memo writer should get the actual option list (or a legality check) before committing to a line.

systematic.pattern: Forge fires instants and abilities in our own draw step or upkeep, and a pass needs a 0.35 lead
systematic.count_or_examples: Assassin's Trophy cast in our DRAW or UPKEEP step: pod01-g3 t12 (GATED p=0.29), pod02-g1 t14 (agreed p=0.65), pod03-g1 t35 (GATED p=0.26; its mana payment also tapped the black sources Wurm needed). Soul-Guide Lantern pop: Jev overruled it 7 times in a row on t11, then the 8th window went through as GATED p=0.41 (pod02-g3 t12).
systematic.why_it_matters: 'Hold interaction for opponents' turns' is the most common memo instruction for removal, and it's the one the asymmetric 0.35 margin makes hardest. Each extra window is another draw from a noisy gate.

systematic.count_or_examples: 'Dalek Drone [P1, 3/3]' shows the controller, not that we own it (pod03-g3 t40). P1's copy of 'Muldrotha, the Gravetide [P1, 6/6]' shares our commander's name (pod03-g1 t27). Commander targets are marked 'commander' but not 'will return to command zone' (Hostage Taker on Hearthhull, pod02-g4 t20; Dellian on Y'shtola, pod01-g2 t36). Walking Ballista options always read '(X=0)'. The memo's Hearthhull-from-exile line was impossible (pod02-g4 t24). No escalation fired when our own Deluge did nothing (pod02-g3 t28), so Jev followed a stale memo.
systematic.why_it_matters: These labels push Jev toward commander-removal tempo plays that reviewers repeatedly flag. The missing 'our wipe fizzled' escalation left one game-relevant memo stale.
